fresh_internal_checks.check: The explicit homogeneous quotient defines a global nonpositive omega-psh potential on normalized projective space; a lies strictly between zero and one.
The analytic pole is exactly one point and has coefficient a in the book logarithm-squared normalization.
The analytic envelope theorem preserves its bounded equivalence class and gives an ordinary analytic ideal model.
Unitary projective transport preserves omega and permutes zero-obstacle envelope competitors, giving distinct single-point model poles.
On every smooth surface modification the pulled-back pole set is a compact analytic fiber, hence closed and locally complete pluripolar.
The preceding closed-pole corollary makes the actual coefficientwise polar restriction closed and positive.
The used support statements and their complete proofs in Demailly Chapter III at pages 141-143 are read; their bidimension-one application eliminates point-supported remainders.
Generic curve coefficients equal a times the divisorial order of the pulled-back point ideal, even when the chosen modification is not a full log resolution.
A fixed compact surface modification has finitely many exceptional curves and their point images; distinct x_j therefore give a finite J_pi.
The pulled-back smooth Kahler form restricts to zero on every curve contracted to a point.
For each coordinate a positive epsilon_pi can satisfy all finitely many j C_pi,j bounds, and is fixed once for the entire sequence.
The form pi*omega + epsilon_pi gamma_pi is strictly positive and Gauduchon because n=2 makes its equation linear; no such claim is silently made in higher dimension.
Degree-one change of variables gives the integral of (pi*omega)^2 equal to one, so every chosen denominator is at least one.
The exact positive polar trace mass is epsilon_pi C_pi,j; coordinates with empty exceptional support have zero polar current.
The bound 1/j is uniform over the entire prescribed set of modifications, so its supremum tends to zero; this does not use a countable detector or a diagonal limit.
The zero model has no polar trace in any coordinate; the comparison still separates analytic models for these choices.
The single-point blowup and resolved pencil give the smooth closed semipositive residual H_a with class H-aE.
For every ordinarily equivalent representative, divisorial removal leaves a bounded residual quasi-psh potential after extension across E.
Bounded products assign zero mass to E and change of variables off E identifies the downstairs non-pluripolar mass with the upstairs bounded residual product.
Closed bounded Bedford--Taylor Stokes and H^2=1, H.E=0, E^2=-1 give mass 1-a^2 for every representative, hence both singularity volumes.
The zero model has volume one and the maximum with p_j is zero, giving upper-volume comparison a^2 in a common positive lower-volume sector.
The result disproves compatibility for arbitrary independent auxiliary choices, not general P01/P17, all choices, model separation or complete metrizability.
